translation:
The TARGET defines four propositions (Def5, Def6, Def7, Def8) in the context of arbitrary types Fm (sentences) and S (proof systems) equipped with logical connectives (including formal implication 🡒, conjunction ⋏, and the biconditional φ 🡘 ψ abbreviating (φ 🡒 ψ) ⋏ (ψ 🡒 φ)), neutral constants (though these are not used in the bodies), and a provability relation 𝓢 ⊢ φ. No axioms are assumed on the proof system 𝓢 (in particular, neither classical propositional logic, nor modus ponens, nor consistency is required), and the operators D, K, T : Fm → Fm are completely arbitrary functions from sentences to sentences.

- Def5 takes a proof system 𝓢 : S and two functions D, K : Fm → Fm, and asserts the meta-level rule: for every sentence φ : Fm, if 𝓢 proves φ and 𝓢 proves D φ, then 𝓢 proves K φ. (The implications here are meta-level, not formal-language implications inside 𝓢.)

- Def6 takes a proof system 𝓢 : S and two functions D, T : Fm → Fm, and asserts: for every sentence φ : Fm, 𝓢 proves the object-language sentence D φ 🡒 (T φ 🡘 φ), i.e., D φ formally implies the conjunction of (T φ 🡒 φ) and (φ 🡒 T φ).

- Def7 takes a proof system 𝓢 : S and two functions D, T : Fm → Fm, and asserts: for every pair of sentences φ, ψ : Fm, 𝓢 proves the object-language biconditional D (φ 🡒 ψ) 🡘 (D φ ⋏ (T φ 🡒 D ψ)), i.e., the formal equivalence between D applied to (φ 🡒 ψ) and the conjunction of D φ with the formal implication from T φ to D ψ.

- Def8 takes a proof system 𝓢 : S and two functions D, K : Fm → Fm, and asserts: for every sentence φ : Fm, 𝓢 proves the object-language biconditional D (K φ) 🡘 D φ, i.e., the conjunction of (D (K φ) 🡒 D φ) and (D φ 🡒 D (K φ)).

divergences.description: In the source, axioms (D4) and (D7) are single universally quantified object-language sentences ((∀x)(∀y)[Sent(x) ∧ Sent(y) → ...] and (∀x)[D(K(x)) ↔ D(x)]), whereas Def7 and Def8 formalize them as meta-level axiom schemas over Fm (∀ φ ψ, 𝓢 ⊢ ... and ∀ φ, 𝓢 ⊢ ...). Proving every sentence-instance is strictly weaker than proving the universally quantified axiom, though this weakening is an expected idealization of the declared abstract setting without quantifiers, arithmetic, or coding. In addition, Def7 omits the Sent(·) guards of (D4) (as declared) and Def8 restricts (D7)'s unguarded quantifier over all objects x to sentences φ : Fm.

In the source, the rule (DK-Intro) has a single conjunctive premise φ ∧ D(φ), whereas Def5 splits it into two separate provability premises (𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ D φ → 𝓢 ⊢ K φ), as noted in the claim. The two forms are equivalent in any classical system such as DTK, though Def5 itself does not include a classical logic hypothesis [Entailment.Cl 𝓢].

In the source, T, K, and D are object-language predicates applied to Gödel codes of sentences in specific arithmetic extensions of PA (DT and DTK), with D(x) defined as T(x) ∨ T(¬x). In the TARGET, T, K, and D are arbitrary independent functions Fm → Fm on an abstract type of sentences (matching the declared abstract setting, though nothing constrains D φ to match T φ ⋎ T (∼φ)).

judgement.summary: Within its declared abstract setting without arithmetic, coding, or object-language quantifiers, the TARGET faithfully captures the propositional structure of (DK-Intro), the conditioned truth biconditional of Theorem 4 / Lemma 7.14.4, axiom (D4), and axiom (D7). The only divergences are minor idealizations inherent to that abstract setting—most notably weakening the universally quantified object-language axioms (D4) and (D7) to meta-level schemas over Fm, splitting the conjunctive premise of (DK-Intro) without assuming classical entailment in the definition itself, and leaving D independent of T.
